items.title: Twelve refusals were filed in Status::note, where the next receipt erases them

must_fix.evidence: A note is one dim row, erased by the next receipt and by a tab switch (Status::clear_note). A refusal there is a refusal the author never sees.

items.title: The file watcher took ResMut<Project> and ResMut<OpenMap> every frame, and Bevy's conflict resolution deferred the badge layout past the frame

must_fix.evidence: The headless suite went from 189 pass / 0 fail to 2-4 failures whose set changed every run. Bisection: watcher disabled -> 189/0 twice; watcher as one system -> 2-4 fail, varying; watcher split into a tick and an act -> 189/0 twice.

items.evidence: crates/bevy_emerge_mapper/src/watch.rs (tick_watch and adopt_changes) and the headless suite

items.title: An agent can drive the editor through typed operations, over MCP, with the file changing under it

must_fix.evidence: Before: the editor's verbs were key handlers, so an agent could only synthesise keystrokes, and a data file edited on disk was invisible until a restart.

items.title: probe reports Ready for any non-loopback host without connecting, so a LAN endpoint that is down is reported ready

must_fix.evidence: probe() answered Reach::Ready for any host not spelled localhost/127./::1, so a LAN endpoint on a closed port was reported ready without a connect. The LAN bind is the documented portable setup; no config makes the preflight run there.

items.title: A map edited on disk reaches the editor's memory but not the screen: the placed pieces are spawned once, at open

must_fix.evidence: Wrong result on screen: the file says the piece moved, the editor's map agrees, the viewport does not (tests/a_map_edited_on_disk_reaches_the_screen.rs failed: 'piece on SCREEN is at Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)'). Common: editing the map file is the hot-reload path. Workaround: restart the editor.

items.title: Undo is declared in the registry and performed by no tool

must_fix.evidence: ops.rs declares Undo::Inverse and Undo::Snapshot, the tool list names the strategy, and no tool performs an undo. The tool descriptions now say so rather than promising one.
